name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default because it reduces eye strain in low-light conditions and aligns with the competitive analysis showing dark themes improve readability and focus in data-heavy interfaces. The trade-off is that some users in bright environments may prefer a light theme, but we mitigate this with a one-click toggle to light mode.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t user preference—it’s that a one-click toggle implies users must *know* their environment will change, then *act* to fix it. Better: default to system preference first, then let users lock a theme if they choose. Settle it by testing both—track how often users manually switch after default exposure.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default but auto-switch to light when the system preference is set to light. This balances eye strain in low light with usability in bright environments without forcing users to manually toggle. The trade-off is a slight delay in first load while checking the system theme, but it removes the cognitive load of users needing to know or remember to switch.

name: Pane
text: The real risk is that auto-switching still assumes users *want* their interface to chase their system—some may prefer a fixed theme regardless of environment. Better: default to system preference, but let users *pre-set* a theme at install; settle it by measuring how often users override the default after first use.
